key_insight: Physics-anchored residual QNNs reduced cloud-cover prediction error versus direct QNNs, but a larger, longer-trained classical model remained more accurate.
engineering_relevance: Learning corrections to a fitted physical estimate can improve compact quantum models within a fixed training budget without replacing the physical baseline.
method: Retain a fitted physical cloud-cover estimate and learn a correction to its logit in transformed target space.
Compare XYZ and ZZXY quantum circuits in six- and eight-input settings using local Z readout and noiseless exact expectations.
Evaluate against compact residual MLP and larger Grundner-Q1 classical references.
evidence_signal: On ICON/DYAMOND-derived data with three matched replicates and 10,000 training samples each, residual QNNs cut test MSE by 38.8–54.3% versus direct QNNs under 30 epochs; residual Q1 achieved MSEs of 0.00778–0.00791 versus 0.01082–0.01124 for residual XYZ.
watch_item: Noiseless offline results establish neither computational quantum advantage nor online climate-model skill.
paper_title: Physics-anchored residual quantum neural networks for cloud-cover parameterization
